first_approach.what: first-approach record: old reference wings at real size, Mach 0.03-0.13 at sea level, -5 to 8 deg, margin 10 % c, tables before the nose fix; upper band 0-85 % c (the same as now)

source: Stage 1 section tables (2-D XFOIL, free transition, N_crit 9; rebuilt 7 Nov 2026 on the fixed nose) through cfdauto.flowmap.engine (strips, uniform elliptic induced angle) in the Re mode of cfdauto.mesh.refine_map; sea level.

as_built.what: decided rules as built (level VC): the largest ring cell over 85-99.5 % c / the station's band cell, max over the stations, per side; reference wing 0 of each type at the four Re levels. And whether writing the upper band as 0-100 % c changes the nodes.

refine_re_transition.png.what: Median transition position over the 65 strips of each type (5 wings × 13 strips) against the root angle, at the four Re levels on the mean chord, upper and lower side, with the decided bands: upper 0–85 % c (shaded: beyond it), lower 0–100 % c.
refine_re_transition.png.conclusion: The upper transition moves aft as the angle and the Re fall: at 10⁵ its median sits at 88–100 % c at −5° on every type, past the upper band's end; the lower transition comes to the leading edge at negative angles (median 0–29 % c at −5°), which the lower band 0–100 % c holds.

refine_re_coverage.png.what: Per type and Re level, −5° to 8°: the share of strips whose band (transition ± 10 % c, bubbles, separation start) fits inside the written upper band 0–85 % c, the share whose transition itself fits (tick), and how far the band's aft end goes past 85 % c.
refine_re_coverage.png.conclusion: As written, the upper band misses the upper transition on most strips at 10⁵ and 3 × 10⁵ (0–49 % fit, short by up to 15 % c, to the trailing edge) and on 3–68 % at 1.5 × 10⁶ and 3 × 10⁶; as built this is no gap, because the shared node distribution (decision 60) and the lower band 0–100 % c already give the upper side band cells to the trailing edge.

refine_re_no_answer.png.what: Share of strips with no XFOIL answer against the root angle, per type and Re level; no strip is below the tables' lowest Re, so each one is beyond the section's 2-D stall or a failed point.
refine_re_no_answer.png.conclusion: Only the tailless wings lose answers in numbers, at negative root angles (up to 46 % of the BWB and 43 % of the flying-wing strips at −5°), where their outboard sections (MH 61, MH 60 / MH 45) are below the lowest angle XFOIL converges at; the band there rests on the other angles.
